chapters.title: Introduction & Foregrounding
chapters.description: Stylistics examines how authors use linguistic devices to make certain parts of a text stand out (foregrounding). The three main mechanisms are Parallelism (identity + contrast), Repetition (emphasis through recurrence), and Deviation (rule-breaking). Deviation is measured either against the text itself (Internal) or against the general language system (External).

chapters.title: Deviation: The Irregularity of Language
chapters.description: Deviation operates across all levels of language. Lexical deviation creates new words (neologisms) via affixation, compounding, or functional conversion. Syntactic deviation alters word order. Phonological deviation includes Aphesis ('gainst), Syncope (o'er), and Apocope (chil). Graphological deviation involves typography. Semantic deviation includes paradox and metaphor.

chapters.title: Cohesion: Making Texts
chapters.description: Cohesion refers to the linguistic ties that connect sentences across sentence boundaries. The four types are: Reference (pronoun substitution), Ellipsis (omitted but understood material), Conjunction (logical connectors), and Lexical Cohesion (related content words). Distinct from Deixis (situational pointing) and Anaphora (within-sentence pro-forms).

chapters.title: Modality and Attitude
topics: Modal Auxiliaries (must, should, may, might, will)
chapters.description: Modality expresses a speaker's commitment, opinion, or attitude. The four parameters are: Probability (might < may < must), Obligation (must/need/should), Willingness (will/would), and Usuality (always/rarely). 'Will' has three uses: Probability, Willingness, and Unmodalized Futurity. Metaphorized modality uses verbs like 'think'/'believe' or phrases like 'it seems'. Generic sentences express timeless truths about categories.

chapters.title: Narrative Structure
chapters.description: Labov identified 6 elements in narrative: Abstract (summary), Orientation (who/when/where), Complicating Action (the indispensable sequence of events), Evaluation (why it's interesting — External commentary vs. Internal woven evaluation), Resolution (what finally happened), and Coda (bridge back to the present). Internal evaluation has 4 types: Intensifying, Comparator, Correlative, and Explicative.

chapters.title: Dialogue and Drama
chapters.description: Discourse analysis examines conversation structure using the Birmingham Model (Exchange > Move > Act). Grice's 4 Maxims underpin cooperative communication; deliberate flouting creates Implicature. Relevance Theory holds that communication succeeds when listeners infer the speaker's intent. Brown & Levinson's politeness framework centres on Face: Positive (desire for approval) and Negative (desire for autonomy). Strategies range from Bald on-record (direct) to Off-record (hinting).

chapters.title: Official Exam: July 2020
chapters.description: The July 2020 exam covers semantic deviation (personification, paradox), syntactic inversion, all four politeness strategies, and Grice's maxim flouting with identification of implicature.

chapters.title: Official Exam: May 2021
chapters.description: The May 2021 exam focuses on identifying modality parameters in context, distinguishing politeness strategies, and analyzing cohesive ties including reference and ellipsis.

chapters.title: Official Exam: June 2022
chapters.description: The June 2022 exam tests deviation identification across levels, politeness strategy selection, and maxim flouting with implicature analysis.

chapters.title: Official Exam: June 2024
chapters.description: The June 2024 exam covers foregrounding devices (parallelism, phonological deviation like syncope/inversion), modality identification, politeness strategies, and narrative element classification.

chapters.title: Official Exam: 2025 (Most Recent)
chapters.description: The most recent past paper before the 2026 cycle. Covers the full curriculum: foregrounding devices, cohesion types, Labov's narrative elements, modality parameters, and discourse analysis.
